body:
## Summary

When an agent-triggered workflow fails before the agent can produce a normal response, the requester may receive no explanation on the issue or PR where they invoked the agent.

This leaves users with a silent failure unless they know to inspect the Actions logs.

## Problem

Some failures happen during setup rather than during the agent's actual response generation, for example:

- provider setup or authentication failures
- runtime/bootstrap failures
- invalid request/envelope metadata
- timeout or infrastructure failures before a response is posted

In these cases, the workflow can fail without posting a user-facing status comment back to the original thread.

## Expected behavior

If an agent workflow fails after accepting a request, it should post a short, sanitized failure notice to the target issue or PR.

The notice should include:

- that the agent could not complete the request
- a broad failure category, if known
- a link to the workflow run for maintainers
- suggested maintainer action when safe to include

The notice should not include secrets, raw environment variables, full stderr dumps, or provider-specific sensitive configuration details.

## Proposed fix

Add a best-effort failure-reporting step/action to agent workflows or to the shared agent runner path. It should run after the agent task fails and post a sanitized comment to the target thread when a target issue or PR is known.

Possible failure categories:

- provider authentication/setup failed
- runtime setup failed
- request metadata validation failed
- agent timed out
- agent exited with an error
- unknown infrastructure failure

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed accepted agent request produces a clear user-facing comment on the target issue/PR.
- The comment is sanitized and does not expose secrets or detailed internal configuration.
- The workflow still fails in Actions so maintainers can investigate.
- The behavior is covered by a regression test or workflow-level test fixture.
title: Post sanitized user-facing comments when accepted agent runs fail before responding
